title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from this page and its neighbours. Grothendieck is building, over a base S_0, a scheme of 'twisted automorphisms' of an extension 𝔊_4^+ of the modular-type group. That group is generated by ρ (order 3) and σ (order 2) modulo a central element ω, with ρ^3 = σ^2 = ω. It acts on a module M on which ρ_M^3 = σ_M^2 = id and 1+ρ_M+ρ_M^2 = 0. The point is to describe such automorphisms algebraically: an automorphism u is determined by u(ρ) = ζρ and u(σ) = η_0 ω^{ν_2/2} σ with ζ, η_0 in M, together with a 'cyclotomic' exponent μ (u_M = μ·id) and two sign characters.

The previous page reduced the relations (47) to the cocycle conditions ζ+ρ(ζ)+ρ^2(ζ) = 0 and η_0+σ(η_0) = 0. This gives a homomorphism u: 𝔊_4^+ → 𝔊_4^+(S_0). What remained were the compatibilities (41) and (42).

This page does (41): u(ε_0) = ε_0^{(μ)} for ε_0 = σρ.
- One computes ε'_0 = η_0 σ(ζ) ω^{ν_2} ε_0.
- Writing μ-1 = 2ν and ν = 2ν' + ν_2, and using ω l_0 χ^{ν_2} = λ_0^{-ν_2}, the condition reduces to η_0 σ(ζ) = λ_0^{(ν)}.
- Apply σ, using σ(η_0) = η_0^{-1}, σ^2(ζ) = ζ and σ(λ_0) = λ_1. This gives ζ = η_0 λ_1(ν), additively ζ = η_0 + ν λ_1. That is exactly the hypothesis (31).
- He also rechecks u(λ_1) = u ρ(λ_0) = ζ ρ(u(λ_0)) = λ_1(μ).

For (42): with u_M = μ·id, one needs u_M to commute with the pairs (ρ_M, ρ'_M) and (σ_M, σ'_M). This is evident, since a scalar commutes with everything.

Conclusion: the groupoid/scheme Z̃_{ρ,σ} is constructed over S_0, with morphisms
- ν' to G_0 (possibly G_a),
- ν_2 to the two-point scheme {0,1}_{S_0},
- an exponent μ = 4ν'+2+ν_2 (reading uncertain),
- sign characters ε_2, ε_3: Z̃ → μ_{S_0} = {±1}.

The next page assembles these into a monomorphism to Aut_gr(𝔊^+) × G_m × μ × μ. It obtains the group structure by schematic density, and an exact sequence with kernel described by explicit linear equations in M × M × G_a.
errors: The transcription writes ξ where the previous page (and the image) has ζ: it is the same element ζ with u(ρ) = ζρ.

Several exponent bookkeeping steps (μ-1 = 2ν, with a struck-out ±1; ν = 2ν'+ν_2 with a struck-out term) were corrected in the manuscript. The final formula μ = 4ν'+2+ν_2 is hard to reconcile with the parity of μ implied by μ-1 = 2ν. This is possibly a misreading, or a minor slip in the conventions.

The notation l_0 versus λ_0 is ambiguous. The underbraces identify l_0^{(2ν')} with λ_0^{2ν'}, so l_0 probably plays the role of a square root of ε_0-type elements. The derivation is consistent once that is granted.

ideas.what: Describing automorphisms of an extension of the (Z/3 * Z/2 type) modular group by a module M through cocycle data (ζ, η_0), satisfying ζ+ρζ+ρ^2ζ = 0 and η_0+ση_0 = 0, plus a 'cyclotomic' scalar μ
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms of group extensions via 1-cocycles; Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type parametrization of automorphisms of the modular group extension
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (group cohomology); in the GT context Drinfeld (1990), Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Theme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, Γ_{1,1}); the details are not published

ideas.what: Making the automorphism data into a group scheme Z̃_{ρ,σ} over S_0, with characters to G_m and μ_2 × μ_2, its group law fixed by schematic density
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic (pro-unipotent/relative-completion style) automorphism group schemes of modular-group extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain–Matsumoto (relative completion), Drinfeld's GRT / pro-unipotent GT

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats the automorphism data of the extension of the modular group as a group scheme over a base S_0. It comes with a cyclotomic character to G_m and sign characters, and its group law is determined by schematic density. This anticipates later algebraic-group models of automorphisms of the modular group (Hain–Matsumoto relative completion, pro-unipotent GT).
missed.quote: Ainsi, le groupoïde Z̃_{ρ,σ} est bel et bien construit
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a modest precursor of scheme-theoretic GT/relative-completion automorphism groups. It may be of historical interest, but the computations themselves are routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification of compatibility conditions (cocycle bookkeeping) inside a longer construction. The only mildly notable feature is the scheme-theoretic packaging of the automorphism group, which is visible more fully on the next page.
transcription_corrections: ξ → ζ throughout (same element as on the previous page).
'Dans [?] ancien ancrage[?]' probably reads 'Dans nos anciennes notations' (with the insertion 'écrivons en termes de u_{G_0} pour simplifier').
'de même[?], on [?] que' in the closing paragraph probably reads 'de même, on trouve que' or similar; 'schéma sur le groupe Z' probably reads 'schéma sur le groupe Z̃ ... des morphismes de schémas'.
